prior_art.basis: Independent review by claude-independent-prior-art-reviewer-20261106: AI commentary exists for highlights and recaps, but no live personal commentator explains games in each viewer's language at scale, so the Main KPI of 2,000,000,000 viewers is unmet. IBM watsonx narrated Masters and Wimbledon highlight clips in English or Spanish, not live play, because generation took seconds to minutes (https://www.nbcnews.com/tech/innovation/us-open-ai-sports-commentary-masters-wimbledon-rcna95244). NBC's AI Al Michaels voice produced about 7 million personalised Olympic recaps, human-reviewed before release (https://tvtechnology.com/news/peacock-to-use-ai-generated-al-michaels-for-recaps-of-olympic-games-highlights). Open live attempts report latency of several seconds that lags play (https://getstream.io/blog/ai-football-commentator-lessons/), while research such as LiveCC reports 0.36 s on a generic benchmark (https://openaccess.thecvf.com/content/CVPR2025/supplemental/Chen_LiveCC_Learning_Video_CVPR_2025_supplemental.pdf). World Cup 2026 broadcasters were only testing adaptive AI commentary (https://publication.aimagazine.com/ai-magazine-june-2026-issue-43/0110591001780301552/p98). Honest limit: recap narration and event-driven text commentary are known answers; live accurate multilingual video commentary is open, and broadcast rights limit deployment.
